story.title: Guinea-Bissau Military Leaders Postpone Elections to 2028
story.summary: Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have announced a two-year delay for presidential and parliamentary elections, now scheduled for November 2028. This decision comes one year after the military took control of the country, with leaders citing insufficient conditions for holding elections at this time.

explore_lenses.label: What exactly changed in the election plan?
explore_lenses.title: A decree replaces the December 2026 vote
explore_lenses.summary: Transitional President Horta Inta-a moved both the presidential and legislative elections from December 6, 2026, to November 26, 2028. The order extends a transition originally framed as one year after the November 26, 2025 coup.

claims.text: Presidential Decree No. 35/2026 revoked the January 21 decree that had set elections for December 6, 2026, and fixed the new date as November 26, 2028.
The postponement applies to both presidential and legislative elections, not solely the presidency.
The prior electoral process was interrupted after the military seized power on November 26, 2025, before official results from the November 23 general election were announced.

points: Presidential Decree No. 35/2026 revoked the January 21 decree that had set elections for December 6, 2026, and fixed the new date as November 26, 2028.
The postponement applies to both presidential and legislative elections, not solely the presidency.
The prior electoral process was interrupted after the military seized power on November 26, 2025, before official results from the November 23 general election were announced.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The decree sets a date but does not publicly provide a detailed, binding sequence of milestones between now and November 2028.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the junta say more time is needed?
explore_lenses.title: Officials cite election readiness and institutional changes
explore_lenses.summary: The transitional authorities say the required technical, material and financial conditions for a credible vote are absent. Earlier reporting identified unfinished party and candidate procedures, while the decree also refers to revisiting the calendar with relevant institutions and stakeholders.

claims.text: The decree says holding the vote without the necessary technical, material and financial conditions could undermine its regularity, transparency, inclusiveness, credibility and public confidence.
On October 8, Prime Minister Ilídio Vieira Té said parties had not held congresses to choose leaders and prospective candidates had missed the October 6 deadline for submissions to the Supreme Court.

The transition had already altered the governing and electoral framework: the UN reported that authorities adopted a new constitution expanding executive powers and revised rules for the electoral commission, parties and electoral code.
The decree calls for reassessing the calendar in coordination with competent institutions and other participants, and references first local elections as part of institutionalizing local government.

explore_lenses.label: Who disputes the transition’s legitimacy?
explore_lenses.title: Opposition and external bodies have challenged the process
explore_lenses.summary: The postponement occurs in a political environment where opposition actors have rejected the transition framework and where external institutions have called for constitutional order and an unhindered electoral process. These positions concern the broader post-coup process, not necessarily a documented response to the November 26 postponement itself.

claims.text: The UN reported that opposition actors rejected the transition framework and the original December 6, 2026 election timetable.

Opposition parties called for a boycott of the August 2026 constitutional referendum, arguing that it would further concentrate power in the presidency; the approved changes weakened the prime minister’s role and cut legislative seats from 102 to 65.

The European Parliament called for restoration of constitutional order, publication of verified 2025 election results without military or political interference, and the release of detained opposition figures.
The military government’s position is that postponement is needed to protect a lawful, transparent and credible electoral process rather than conduct a vote without adequate preparation.

story_report.summary: Guinea-Bissau’s military leaders have postponed presidential and legislative elections from Dec. 6, 2026, to Nov. 26, 2028, extending the transition by nearly two years. The decision, announced on the first anniversary of the military takeover, was formalized by a decree that revoked the previous election date. The authorities say the delay is needed because conditions are not yet in place for a regular, transparent and credible vote.

sections.heading: Military takeover halted electoral process
sections.body: The earlier electoral process was interrupted when the military seized power on Nov. 26, 2025, before official results from the Nov. 23 general election were announced. During the transition, authorities adopted a new constitution that expanded executive powers and revised rules governing the electoral commission, political parties and the electoral code. The decree also refers to reassessing the calendar with relevant institutions and participants, including plans for initial local elections tied to establishing local government.

sections.heading: Opposition challenges transition framework
sections.body: Opposition actors had already rejected the transition framework and the original December 2026 timetable, according to the United Nations. Opposition parties also urged a boycott of the August 2026 constitutional referendum, saying it would further concentrate presidential power; the approved changes weakened the prime minister’s role and reduced legislative seats from 102 to 65. The European Parliament has called for constitutional order to be restored, verified 2025 election results to be published without interference, and detained opposition figures to be released.

unresolved.text: Authorities have set the November 2028 date but have not publicly provided a detailed binding timetable, itemized budget, operational plan or independently verified benchmarks for determining when electoral conditions have been met.
The consulted material did not identify comprehensive, on-the-record responses to the Nov. 26, 2026 decree from all major parties, ECOWAS or the African Union.

related_stories.title: Pittsburgh Steelers Release Aaron Rodgers Following Criticism of Coach
related_stories.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have released quarterback Aaron Rodgers shortly after he publicly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on 'The Pat McAfee Show.' Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and missing walkthroughs, leading to tensions within the team. Steelers president Art Rooney II stated that 'insubordination will not be tolerated' in light of the incident.

related_stories.title: FIFA Reports Cyberattack Targeting Personal and Business Information
related_stories.summary: FIFA has confirmed that it was the target of a cyberattack that accessed a limited set of personal and business information. The attack comes at a challenging time for the organization and its president, Gianni Infantino. The hacking group responsible for the breach is identified as the 'Handsome Boy Hacking Club.'

related_stories.title: Kim Jong Un Promises to Expand North Korea's Nuclear Arsenal Amid U.S. Tensions
related_stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has vowed to increase the country's nuclear weapons production in response to perceived threats from the United States and South Korea. This announcement follows his recent disregard for an overture from U.S. President Donald Trump to meet during Trump's visit to Asia. Kim visited facilities involved in producing nuclear materials, emphasizing the need to bolster North Korea's military capabilities.
